title: Outbreak Control: Quarantine Protocol
description: Lead the public health response to a dangerous outbreak! Place quarantine zones to contain the spread of infection across a population grid. Every move teaches real epidemiology concepts — from containment strategy and contact tracing to herd immunity and resource allocation under pressure.
learning_objectives: Understand how infectious diseases spread through populations
Learn containment strategies: quarantine zones, buffer areas, and isolation
Practice resource allocation under time pressure and uncertainty
Explore the tradeoffs between aggressive containment and community impact
Develop spatial reasoning about how outbreaks propagate geographically
Understand the importance of early intervention in epidemic response
how_to_play: You and the AI take turns placing markers on a 9x9 population grid. You place Quarantine Zones to contain the outbreak; the AI spreads Infection.
Surround empty intersections with your quarantine zones to claim that territory as safe — protected population under your watch.
If you completely surround a cluster of Infection markers (no empty adjacent spaces), those infections are eradicated — containment success!
The Ko rule prevents you from immediately re-quarantining a just-released zone, simulating the delay in redeploying health resources.
The game ends when both sides pass consecutively, meaning the outbreak has stabilized.
Your score is safe territory plus eradicated infections. The AI gets a 6.5 point komi bonus. Protect more of the population than the infection claims to win!

storybook_pages.title: Outbreak Alert
storybook_pages.text: A novel pathogen has emerged in the region. As the chief epidemiologist, you must deploy quarantine zones across the population grid to stop the spread. But the infection is aggressive — it's racing to claim territory of its own. Every intersection represents a community, and every move you make determines who stays safe and who falls to the outbreak.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: public health command center with a large grid map showing green quarantine shields and red infection markers, doctors and scientists working urgently, dramatic lighting, cartoon style, medical theme

storybook_pages.title: Containment Strategy
storybook_pages.text: Effective containment isn't about blocking every single path — it's about surrounding the infection. Create buffer zones around vulnerable populations. Cut off supply routes the pathogen uses to spread. And remember: if you can completely encircle a cluster of infections, you can eradicate it entirely. Think like an epidemiologist — every zone placement is a strategic decision.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: diagram showing quarantine zones forming barriers around red infection clusters on a grid, arrows showing how containment works, green shields protecting communities, educational cartoon style

storybook_pages.title: Flatten the Curve
storybook_pages.text: As the grid fills up, the battle intensifies. Some areas are lost to infection, but you can still protect the majority. Sometimes retreating from one zone lets you secure a larger safe region. The best public health response isn't about winning everywhere — it's about saving the most lives with the resources you have.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: aerial view of a population grid with green safe zones and red infected areas, a large curved graph overlay showing 'flattening the curve', hopeful sunrise in background, cartoon medical style

rounds.coaching_moment: Think carefully about the trade-offs before committing to this path.
rounds.reflection_prompt: Why did you make this choice?

transfer_exercises: Apply outbreak containment logic to managing a viral social media crisis — identify index cases (first posts), trace spread patterns, and quarantine misinformation at source.
Use the herd immunity threshold concept when driving organisational change: you don't need 100% buy-in — reaching ~70% adoption creates peer pressure that brings the rest along.

glossary_terms.definition: The average number of people one infected person will pass a disease to in a fully susceptible population. R0 > 1 means exponential spread; R0 < 1 means the outbreak dies out.
When enough of a population is immune that disease transmission is blocked even for non-immune individuals — typically 60–90% depending on R0.
Identifying and monitoring people who have been exposed to an infectious disease to break transmission chains before symptoms appear.
Quarantine separates those who may have been exposed; isolation separates those who are confirmed infected. Both are distinct containment tools.
A graph showing disease case counts over time — the shape reveals whether an outbreak is a point source, propagated, or intermittent.

cultural_context: India's experience with COVID-19, dengue, and periodic disease outbreaks has highlighted the importance of public health strategy. Understanding containment logic helps future Indian health professionals and policy-makers respond more effectively to disease threats.
reflection_prompt: Where did you trade influence for territory? Was it worth it?
